title: FastAPI response filters are opted in by endpoint function, not by HTTP method
answers: why does my POST route not get its response filtered
how do I add response filtering to a FastAPI route under basic-auth
response filter ignored for POST endpoints
register a response filter for a FastAPI endpoint
body:
Invariant: a FastAPI route gets a response filter only if its endpoint function object is a key in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS.
mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_find_fastapi_response_filter takes only the request and resolves request.scope['endpoint']; the former GET-only gate was removed, so a POST collection route such as job_api.py:search_jobs is filtered when registered.
fastapi_permission_middleware applies the filter only when the user is not an admin and response.status_code < 400, after buffering the body iterator.
Skipping registration leaves the route returning the unfiltered handler result, with no error raised.
applies: Any new or existing FastAPI route under basic-auth that returns a collection of user-scoped resources; does not cover Flask routes.
says: Non-admin users can see jobs belonging to other accounts in search results.
The jobs search screen displays records that standard accounts lack permission to view.
Regular users should only see their own jobs when searching the jobs list.
Ensure searching jobs hides items created by other users from non-admin members.
Unauthorized background jobs appear in search results for users who are not administrators.
search: FastAPI routes under basic-auth receive response filtering only when their endpoint function object is registered in FASTAPI_ENDPOINT_RESPONSE_FILTERS. In mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py, _find_fastapi_response_filter resolves request.scope['endpoint'] without a GET-only restriction, allowing POST collection endpoints like job_api.py:search_jobs to be filtered. fastapi_permission_middleware applies filters only for non-admin users when response.status_code is under 400 after buffering the body iterator, while unregistered routes silently return unfiltered results. Applies to FastAPI routes returning collections of user-scoped resources under basic-auth, excluding Flask routes.
